utterances.text: But you have not given any information with regard to identity of Witness O to the defence is what I hear from Ms. McMurrey.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, informed of the identity of -- I think maybe -- we are talking about Mr. Brackovic, who is still the lead counsel for Mr. Esad Landzo, as far as I can understand. He told us at 2 o'clock yesterday that he was going to tell Mr. Ackerman. What happens by way of that I do not know, of course, but we try to do our best to give you all the information you may need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Now bearing all that in mind, are you prepared to argue the question of the protection? . If you are, then --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, we would be happy to argue the issue of the protection, but we are not prepared at this moment to go forward with the cross-examination of a witness who we are caught by surprise on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I maintain, your Honours, to say that we are not doing this on surprise. We have had this witness on the list as number 12. We have informed them yesterday that he has asked for protection and divulged to the lead counsel who he is. I am quite prepared to go into a hearing about the protection which he has asked for, which for my part consists of the concerns that he gave me when he met me the day before yesterday, and then I immediately filed a motion. I feel an obligation to protect the witnesses we call before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: We are not contesting maybe there is a valid reason for protection. What I would like the record to reflect and the Trial Chamber to understand is if Mr. Brackovic was given notice yesterday, it may be constructive notice for us, but we did not receive actual notice of this change in the schedule until 9.45 this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I think, your Honour, Ms. McHenry has some information to add to this which I have not been provided with.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Because I am sitting down and I can look at the documents, I just want to point out it is the case on the modified witness list Mr. Bart d'Hooge was the next witness and the witness after that was this witness, Witness O. It is always going to be the case, as my counsel has said, that there is going to be some change in witnesses because of availability. The fact that this witness has now been moved up one position, I do not think that defence counsel could say they could never be prepared to cross-examine. On behalf of all the prosecution, we will state that we are sure that this is not the last time this is going to happen. It is an incredibly difficult situation -- Mr. Turone knows more about it than I do -- to try to get the witnesses here. We act in good faith. We tell the defence attorneys as soon as we know. The fact that someone has been moved up one spot versus the other we do not believe can be any grounds for defence counsel to argue they are unprepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am certainly prepared at this point on behalf of Mr. Landzo at least to accede to a new Rule, that new Rule being from this day forward we implicitly have notice from the prosecution that they may call any one of the next two or three witnesses so we can be prepared for as many as two or three at a time. It is not my understanding that that had been the Rule up to this point. Whether or not we should have had notice, whether or not we should have known is really beside the point. The position we are in right now is we are not prepared to conduct the cross-examination of this witness today. We have just been handed a significant amount of material just this morning at 9.45 regarding what this witness did. The witness obviously, now that he has been identified to us, is a doctor who conducted medical examinations and is apparently coming here to testify about the results of his medical examinations. Now how that cannot be an expert witness I have no idea, because were it not for his medical training, he would not be permitted to testify about the medical opinions that he has given here. So by definition he is an expert. We have not had the proper designation of this witness as an expert witness. So I have a proposal for the Trial Chamber: first of all, that the Trial Chamber make whatever decision the Trial Chamber might think is appropriate regarding the failure to designate this witness as an expert witness; second of all, that we adjourn the proceedings until 10 o'clock in the morning, when they can go ahead and put on their witness. By that time if the witness is going to be called, in spite of the fact they failed to designate him as expert, then we can be prepared not only for that witness certainly but for the two following on the list. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): May I ask your Honours to rule also on the fact that our learned colleague, Madame McHenry, referred to. Is it possible for the defence to be informed of a change in the list of witnesses by telephone on the eve of the testimony of the witness? Ms. McHenry said previously that the prosecution wanted to ensure a fair trial. Information given by telephone at 4.00 pm on a Sunday for preparations for the cross-examination of a witness who was previously put on the list in my view does not contribute to that goal. I therefore also ask the Trial Chamber to rule particularly because we have been told there will be more such cases in the future. I think that we need to know exactly the position of the Trial Chamber, that is that no changes can be made in the list of witnesses within such a short time period that will put them in a position not to be able to carry out the cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I wonder whether I can add something? I was in Vienna yesterday. The knowledge that this witness was to be called this morning arrived in my little brain at about 9.30 this morning. Shortly after that this document was brought in by the representative of the prosecution. It is true that we have what looks like a similar document in Serbo-Croat with all sorts of very interesting stamps and so on all over it. My fellow counsel and I have not had an opportunity for a moment to compare whether this document bears any relationship whatever with what has been served on us previously. There are but 24 hours in the day, your Honours, and those 24 hours are occupied with other things. As your Honours will be aware, I have just come back from preparing the matter that we were speaking about before the adjournment. Although it may well be, and I am not sure at the moment, that I do not have a great number of questions for this witness, one of the duties of counsel is to -- in a case of this kind, where there are so many documents that appear in either Serbo-Croat or English, and have to be translated, it is one of our duties to check that the English version bears some resemblance to the Serbo-Croat version. It would be quite wrong if the court were to admit one of the entries in here was a bad translation of the Serbo-Croat. It would be an appalling injustice if that was to be allowed in evidence without us having an opportunity to check the two documents match one another. If someone can tell me how we can do that in fifteen minutes before coming into court, then they might like to patent it and sell it on the open market. It is just not possible to do that checking process and to prepare a proper cross-examination if errors are found. That is the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Your Honour, not to prolong this debate, I again just have to stress that as to disclosure we have done all we can. It is absolutely not right when Mr. Ackerman says there has not been a notice. We cannot control the communication between lead counsel and other counsel on the side of the defence, and it is a Ruling by this trial that serving documents in the language of the defence lawyers and the accused, namely in Serbo-Croat, is sufficient. They have been on notice that this witness is going to be called a long time. He is on our list as number 12, and I can read what is said in the -- what it is all about: "Physician. He visited and issued medical certificates on a number of former detainees", etc, etc. I can disclose that without disclosing his identity. So service has been done, and if there is miscommunication between counsels of different languages posed to me, I cannot cure that thing, and I have told your Honours that full disclosure has been done. The name is on the list. Yesterday they have been informed what is going to happen and everybody knows what is going to happen. This is, in my submission, not a surprise witness. We are doing our best and I have had severe trouble to bring this gentleman to The Hague at all and even had to promise him that he could return reasonably. Thank you very much, your Honours. I have nothing more to add. I am prepared to move on to the protection question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: The contention is that serving them with the papers this morning is sufficient notice?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: No. They have been served with these documents months ago, months ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What are the papers you are serving this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: As a service to them in a clear English translation of the documents they have had for a very long time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What you served long ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Long ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: This is the translation that the court is going to be using. Unless your Honours have suddenly developed a sudden taste for the Serbo-Croat language you are going to be using this, the English version; that was served on us at 9.45. We have not checked it to see whether it is authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not think we have even gotten yet to the initial question of the prosecution says this guy is just a fact witness. If he is a physician and he is going to be testifying about diagnoses, about things that require special expertise and training, he is not a fact witness; he is an expert. Physicians can testify about a whole lot of things. They can testify about traffic accidents they saw and that makes them fact witnesses but the minute they start saying: "I examined this person and he had X", they stop being fact witnesses and start becoming expert witnesses because you have their special training and expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: There are three issues here. I can see perhaps serving papers this morning and arguing it is one -- almost this morning must be precipitant but possibly you could still argue the question of the protection, which is a different matter. So after that we can talk about whether the witness can be available to you, because even if he testifies, it might take some time before we get to the conclusion of it, before cross-examination arises. It might not be today. So you still have time to look at some of those things. So I suppose we can go ahead and discuss the question of the protection. The protection is in private, so we can do that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Pages 2798 to 2808 in closed session
